reason: The `adapter_name` read that selects the adapter-specific schema still happens, one frame down: loadSchema delegates that arm to loadAdapterSpecificSchema, which trails must also call on its own from test-setup-dy.ts (the per-worker schema load runs through DatabaseTasks, not through loadSchema). The wide ratchet is lexical per method, so the extraction reads as an omitted call.

`File.exist?(adapter_specific_schema_file)` asks whether a Ruby schema file is on disk. trails resolves adapter-specific schemas through the ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_SCHEMAS lookup instead of the filesystem, so the presence check is a key lookup, not a stat.

Ruby's Kernel#load evaluates schema.rb as source. trails' mirror of schema.rb is the canonical registry, so loading it means laying that registry onto the adapter — `loadCanonicalSchema(adapter)`. No JS analogue of `load` exists.
`StringIO.new` backs the `$stdout` silencing around Ruby's `load`, which prints a migration line per statement. Laying the schema through the adapter prints nothing, so there is no output to silence.
